source_text:
ὁρωμένου σώματος τῆς θεότητος ὑπεραίρων ἐνεργείᾳ.
βʹ. Μὴ ἀπατάτωσαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, μηδὲ ἀπατάσθωσαν ἄνθρωπον ἄνουν
δεχόμενοι τὸν κυριακὸν, ὡς αὐτοὶ λέγουσι, μᾶλλον δὲ τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν καὶ Θεόν·
οὐδὲ γὰρ τὸν ἄνθρωπον χωρίζομεν τῆς θεότητος, ἀλλ' ἕνα καὶ τὸν αὐτὸν
δογματίζομεν, πρότερον μὲν οὐκ ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ Θεὸν καὶ μόνον Υἱὸν καὶ
προαιώνιον ἀμιγῆ σώματος καὶ τῶν ὅσα σώματος· ἐπὶ τέλει δὲ καὶ ἄνθρωπον
προσληφθέντα ὑπὲρ τῆς ἡμετέρας σωτηρίας, παθητὸν σαρκὶ, ἀπαθῆ θεότητι,
περιγραπτὸν σώματι, ἀπερίγραπτον θεότητι, τὸν αὐτὸν ἐπίγειον καὶ οὐράνιον,
thought_title: One and the same: God and man, not a mindless man
orientation: Cyril continues his argument against Theodore's party, insisting that Christ is one and the same both God and man, not a mindless man.
pass_a_gloss: of the visible body, exalting the divinity by activity. 2. Let not the people deceive, nor let them be deceived, accepting the Lord as a mindless man, as they themselves say, but rather our Lord and God; for neither do we separate the man from the divinity, but we teach one and the same, formerly not man, but God and only Son and pre-eternal, unmixed with body and with the things of body; but at the end also man, assumed for our salvation, passible in flesh, impassible in divinity, circumscribed in body, uncircumscribed in divinity, the same earthly and heavenly,

choices.why: Glossary term for Theodore's alleged teaching; keeps the literal sense of a human being without the divine mind.
Literal rendering of the adjective κυριακός, referring to the man belonging to the Lord; preserves the possessive force.
Renders the verb's doctrinal force plainly; 'we teach as doctrine' is in the gloss, but 'we teach' is the clean literal choice.
Literal compound: before the ages; matches the brief's description of the Word existing before the ages.
Literal rendering of the adjective with genitive; preserves the sense of no mixture with body.
Glossary term for the flesh or humanity assumed by the Word.

pass_b_english: the visible body, while exalting it by the energy of his divinity.

Let no one deceive, and let no one be deceived, by accepting the Lord as a mindless man, as they themselves say—or rather, our Lord and God. For we do not separate the man from the divinity, but we teach that he is one and the same: first not a man, but God and only Son, pre-eternal, unmixed with body and with all that belongs to body; and at the end also a man, assumed for our salvation, passible in flesh, impassible in divinity, circumscribed in body, uncircumscribed in divinity—the same one earthly and heavenly,

problems.why: 'κυριακόν' is substantival 'the Lord' or 'the one belonging to the Lord', not 'the Lord's man'. The English adds 'man' not in source, changing meaning.
problems.fix: the Lord, as they themselves say—or rather, our Lord and God
problems.ruling: τὸν κυριακὸν is substantival adjective 'the Lord's one/what belongs to the Lord'; adding 'man' imports ἄνθρωπον, changing meaning.

edits.old: the Lord's man as a mindless man
edits.new: the Lord as a mindless man

problems.why: Same Greek concept rendered two ways; reader may miss connection.
Three different renderings for same theological concept of Word becoming flesh.

problems.quote: as they themselves say—or rather, our Lord and God
problems.why: Unclear who 'they' refers to; Theodore's followers? The phrase 'or rather' suggests Cyril correcting himself mid-polemic.
problems.fix: Add note identifying 'they' as Theodore's party.

problems.quote: first not a man, but God and only Son, pre-eternal, unmixed with body and with all that belongs to body; and at the end also a man
problems.why: Chronologically confusing: 'first...at the end' suggests temporal sequence in Christ's life, but means 'in logical priority' versus 'in incarnation'.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'first in order of being...finally in the economy of incarnation.'

problems.why: Reader cannot tell who 'they' are—Theodore's followers? The reader needs to know whose view is being rejected.
problems.fix: Identify 'they' as Theodore and his supporters.

problems.quote: circumscribed in body, uncircumscribed in divinity
problems.why: 'Circumscribed' is technical theological jargon meaning 'limited/spatially bounded'; unexplained for a general reader.
problems.fix: Use 'bounded in body, unbounded in divinity' or add a gloss.

edits.old: first not a man, but God and only Son, pre-eternal, unmixed with body and with all that belongs to body; and at the end also a man
edits.new: first in order of being not a man, but God and only Son, pre-eternal, unmixed with body and with all that belongs to body; and finally in the economy of the incarnation also a man

edits.old: circumscribed in body, uncircumscribed in divinity
edits.new: bounded in body, unbounded in divinity

fixed: The glossary problem about 'mindless man' is not a real issue in the English: the phrase appears once as 'mindless man' and is consistent with the glossary. The gloss had 'the Lord's man as a mindless man', which is now corrected to match the English.

The glossary problem about 'enfleshed' is not applicable: the English does not use 'enfleshed' anywhere; the concept is rendered as 'assumed for our salvation' and 'incarnation' in the edit, which is consistent.

The speaker problem about 'as they themselves say—or rather, our Lord and God' is not a real issue: the phrase 'as they themselves say' clearly refers to Theodore's party, who are the opponents being refuted, and 'or rather' is Cyril's rhetorical correction. No change needed.

The speaker problem about 'as they themselves say' is not a real issue: the context makes clear that 'they' are those who accept the Lord as a mindless man, i.e., Theodore's followers. No change needed.

last_rejected.quote: and at the end also a man, assumed for our salvation
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπὶ τέλει δὲ καὶ ἄνθρωπον προσληφθέντα ὑπὲρ τῆς ἡμετέρας σωτηρίας
last_rejected.why: Missing 'assumed'—wait, 'assumed' is present. Let me recheck: English has 'assumed'. Good.
last_rejected.ruling: Self-corrected: 'assumed' is present in English for προσληφθέντα. No actual omission.

last_rejected.quote: Let no one deceive, and let no one be deceived
last_rejected.source_quote: Μὴ ἀπατάτωσαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, μηδὲ ἀπατάσθωσαν
last_rejected.why: Third person plural imperatives: 'Let men not deceive, nor let them be deceived.' English 'no one' loses the plural 'men/people' and makes it impersonal.
last_rejected.fix: Let people not deceive, nor let them be deceived
last_rejected.ruling: οἱ ἄνθρωποι = 'men/people'; 'no one' is acceptable impersonal rendering of third-person imperative prohibition.

last_rejected.quote: exalting it by the energy of his divinity
last_rejected.why: Source says 'exalting by energy/power,' not 'by the energy of his divinity.' The genitive 'τῆς θεότητος' goes with 'ὑπεραίρων' (exalting the body above the divinity? No—wait: 'ὁρωμένου σώματος τῆς θεότητος ὑπεραίρων ἐνεργείᾳ' = 'of the visible body, exalting [it] above the divinity by energy'? Actually this is fragmentary. The English adds 'his divinity' and 'it' not clearly in source. But this is a fragment, so context is unclear. Let me re-read: 'the visible body, while exalting it by the energy of his divinity'—this seems to add 'his' and interpret ἐνεργείᾳ as 'energy of his divinity.' The source has no 'his.'
last_rejected.fix: the visible body, exalting [it] by power
last_rejected.ruling: Fragmentary context; τῆς θεότητος likely governs ἐνεργείᾳ. 'his' is natural pronominal gloss, not a major error.
